gloss: to tell; to inform; to announce

definitions.gloss: to tell; to inform; to announce
definitions.explanation: To communicate important information or news to someone. Has a somewhat formal or literary tone and often implies delivering significant or weighty news.
Used figuratively when something signals or marks the beginning or end of a period, season, or event.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}が{患者|かんじゃ}に{結果|けっか}を{告|つ}げた。
examples.english: The doctor told the patient the results.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{覚悟|かくご}を{決|き}めて、{家族|かぞく}に{真実|しんじつ}を{告|つ}げた。
examples.english: Having made up his mind, he told his family the truth.

examples.japanese: {鐘|かね}の{音|おと}が{正午|しょうご}を{告|つ}げた。
{桜|さくら}が{春|はる}の{訪|おとず}れを{告|つ}げる。
examples.english: The cherry blossoms herald the arrival of spring.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}{終了|しゅうりょう}のホイッスルが{鳴|な}り、{長|なが}いシーズンの{終|お}わりを{告|つ}げた。
examples.english: The final whistle blew, signaling the end of the long season.

notes:
More literary and formal than {言|い}う or {伝|つた}える. Often used in set phrases and for emotionally significant or weighty communication. The expression {別|わか}れを{告|つ}げる (to bid farewell) is particularly common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{別|わか}れを{告|つ}げる: to bid farewell
・{真実|しんじつ}を{告|つ}げる: to tell the truth
・{終|お}わりを{告|つ}げる: to signal the end
・{春|はる}を{告|つ}げる: to herald spring
